chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abi al-Qasim, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said: I asked him about a man who stole, so he said:

I heard my father عليه السلام saying: 'In his time, 'Ali عليه السلام was brought a man who had stolen, so he cut off his hand. Then he was brought again a second time, so he cut off his foot from the opposite side. Then he was brought a third time, so he kept him permanently in prison and spent on him from the treasury of the Muslims. And he said: Thus did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم act; I do not oppose him.'

key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.رِجْلَهُ مِنْ خِلَافٍ: his foot from the opposite side, indicating cross-amputation
key_terms.فَخَلَّدَهُ السِّجْنَ: he kept him permanently in prison
key_terms.فَقَطَعَ يَدَهُ: he cut off his hand as the prescribed punishment
key_terms.لَا أُخَالِفُهُ: I do not oppose him, meaning adherence to the practice of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for repeated theft according to Imam 'Ali عليه السلام in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling for repeated theft as practiced by Imam 'Ali عليه السلام in accordance with the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It describes escalating punishment for the first and second offenses, followed by permanent imprisonment and maintenance from the public treasury upon the third offense.
